Description: Correlations among 14 ability tests for 355 school children, the bi-factor example of Holzinger & Swineford (1937).
Reference: Holzinger, K. J., & Swineford, F. (1937). The bi-factor method. Psychometrika, 2, 41-54.
Notes: Covariance layout (irw_cov). Script data/covariance/pilot_rpackages.R. Taken from psychTools::Holzinger (package transcription, not verified against the paper); reshaped to the long lower triangle on 2026-11-17, values unchanged.

Description: Harman's '24 psychological variables': correlations among 24 ability tests for 145 Grant-White pupils (Holzinger & Swineford, 1939).
Reference: Holzinger, K. J., & Swineford, F. (1939). A study in factor analysis: The stability of a bi-factor solution. Supplementary Educational Monographs, 48.
Notes: Covariance layout (irw_cov). Script data/covariance/pilot_rpackages.R. Taken from datasets::Harman74.cor (package transcription, not verified against the paper); reshaped to the long lower triangle on 2026-11-17, values unchanged.

Description: The classic nine-test Holzinger-Swineford correlation matrix (visual, verbal, speed) for 145 Grant-White pupils; the LISREL NPV.KM example.
Reference: Holzinger, K. J., & Swineford, F. (1939). A study in factor analysis: The stability of a bi-factor solution. Supplementary Educational Monographs, 48.
Notes: Covariance layout (irw_cov). Script data/covariance/pilot_rpackages.R. Taken from psychTools::Holzinger.9 (package transcription, not verified against the paper); reshaped to the long lower triangle on 2026-11-17, values unchanged. Subset of holzinger_1939_grantwhite24's sample.

Description: Correlations among nine ability tests (213 high-school students), McDonald's selection from Thurstone & Thurstone (1941) via Bechtoldt sample 2.
Reference: Thurstone, L. L., & Thurstone, T. G. (1941). Factorial studies of intelligence. University of Chicago Press.
Notes: Covariance layout (irw_cov). Script data/covariance/pilot_rpackages.R. Taken from psychTools::Thurstone (package transcription, not verified against the paper); reshaped to the long lower triangle on 2026-11-17, values unchanged. Subset of bechtoldt_1961_ability17 group sample2.

Description: Correlations among 17 Thurstone ability tests in two samples of high-school students (N = 212 and 213), from Bechtoldt's (1961) factor-stability study.
Reference: Bechtoldt, H. P. (1961). An empirical study of the factor analysis stability hypothesis. Psychometrika, 26, 405-432.
Notes: Covariance layout (irw_cov). Script data/covariance/pilot_rpackages.R. Taken from psychTools::Bechtoldt.1 / Bechtoldt.2 (package transcription, not verified against the paper); reshaped to the long lower triangle on 2026-11-17, values unchanged.

Description: Correlations among nine College Board examination scores, separately for boys (N = 4,175) and girls (N = 2,899), from Brigham (1932).
Reference: Brigham, C. C. (1932). A study of errors. College Entrance Examination Board.
Notes: Covariance layout (irw_cov). Script data/covariance/pilot_rpackages.R. Taken from psychTools::Thurstone.33 (package transcription, not verified against the paper); reshaped to the long lower triangle on 2026-11-17, values unchanged.

Description: Correlations among nine ability tests (N = 710) used by Tucker (1958) to introduce inter-battery factor analysis.
Reference: Tucker, L. R. (1958). An inter-battery method of factor analysis. Psychometrika, 23, 111-136.
Notes: Covariance layout (irw_cov). Script data/covariance/pilot_rpackages.R. Taken from psychTools::Tucker (package transcription, not verified against the paper); reshaped to the long lower triangle on 2026-11-17, values unchanged. Nine variables from Thurstone & Thurstone (1941).

Description: Correlations among eight physical measurements (height, arm span, weight, chest girth, ...) for 305 girls aged 7-17 (Mullen, 1939; Harman Table 2.3).
Reference: Mullen, F. (1939). Factors in the growth of girls seven to seventeen years of age. Unpublished doctoral dissertation, University of Chicago.
Notes: Covariance layout (irw_cov). Script data/covariance/pilot_rpackages.R. Taken from datasets::Harman23.cor (package transcription, not verified against the paper); reshaped to the long lower triangle on 2026-11-17, values unchanged.

Description: Burt's correlations among 11 emotional traits for 172 children; not positive definite as published.
Reference: Burt, C. (1916). General and specific factors underlying the primary emotions. Report of the British Association for the Advancement of Science, 85th meeting, 694-696.
Notes: Covariance layout (irw_cov). Script data/covariance/pilot_rpackages.R. Taken from psychTools::burt (package transcription, not verified against the paper); reshaped to the long lower triangle on 2026-11-17, values unchanged. Not positive definite as published; Sorrow-Tenderness .87 is probably a typo for .81 (psychTools::burt), kept as published.

Description: Correlations among 16 health-outcome items (N = 35,000) from Reise, Morizot & Hays (2007), a bifactor example.
Reference: Reise, S. P., Morizot, J., & Hays, R. D. (2007). The role of the bifactor model in resolving dimensionality issues in health outcomes measures. Quality of Life Research, 16, 19-31.
Notes: Covariance layout (irw_cov). Script data/covariance/pilot_rpackages.R. Taken from psychTools::Reise (package transcription, not verified against the paper); reshaped to the long lower triangle on 2026-11-17, values unchanged. Source given in psychTools as personal communication from S. Reise.

Description: Covariance matrix of six ability and timed-performance tests for 112 people (Smith & Stanley, 1983); R's ability.cov.
Reference: Smith, G. A., & Stanley, G. (1983). Clocking g: Relating intelligence and measures of timed performance. Intelligence, 7, 353-368.
Notes: Covariance layout (irw_cov). Script data/covariance/pilot_rpackages.R. Taken from datasets::ability.cov (package transcription, not verified against the paper); reshaped to the long lower triangle on 2026-11-17, values unchanged. Covariance matrix; the package's centre vector is all zeros, so no means are given.

Description: Covariance matrix of 18 quality-of-life measures (N = 403) from Chen, West & Sousa (2006), comparing bifactor and second-order models.
Reference: Chen, F. F., West, S. G., & Sousa, K. H. (2006). A comparison of bifactor and second-order models of quality of life. Multivariate Behavioral Research, 41, 189-225.
Notes: Covariance layout (irw_cov). Script data/covariance/pilot_rpackages.R. Taken from psych::Chen (package transcription, not verified against the paper); reshaped to the long lower triangle on 2026-11-17, values unchanged. Covariance matrix.

Description: Multitrait-multimethod correlations: 111 supervisors rated on seven dimensions via their least and most effective subordinate (14 variables).
Reference: Boruch, R. F., Larkin, J. D., Wolins, L., & MacKinney, A. C. (1970). Alternative methods of analysis: Multitrait-multimethod data. Educational and Psychological Measurement, 30, 833-853.
Notes: Covariance layout (irw_cov). Script data/covariance/batch_rpackages2.R. Taken from fungible::Boruch70 (package transcription, not verified against the paper); reshaped to the long lower triangle on 2026-11-17, values unchanged. Multitrait-multimethod: 7 dimensions x 2 sources (X = least, Y = most effective subordinate).

Description: Correlations among 12 associative-learning task scores (free recall, serial learning, paired associates) for 97 participants.
Reference: Malmi, R. A., Underwood, B. J., & Carroll, J. B. (1979). The interrelationships among some associative learning tasks. Bulletin of the Psychonomic Society, 13(3), 121-123. https://doi.org/10.3758/BF03335032
Notes: Covariance layout (irw_cov). Script data/covariance/batch_rpackages2.R. Taken from fungible::Malmi79 (package transcription, not verified against the paper); reshaped to the long lower triangle on 2026-11-17, values unchanged. Free recall (FR), serial learning (SL) and paired-associate (PA) tasks.

Description: Covariance matrix of state and trait anxiety and anger for 684 female students, from Cox & Wermuth (1996).
Reference: Cox, D. R., & Wermuth, N. (1996). Multivariate dependencies: Models, analysis and interpretation. Chapman and Hall.
Notes: Covariance layout (irw_cov). Script data/covariance/batch_rpackages2.R. Taken from ggm::anger (package transcription, not verified against the paper); reshaped to the long lower triangle on 2026-11-17, values unchanged. Covariance matrix; X = anxiety state, Y = anger state, Z = anxiety trait, U = anger trait (ggm help page); the study that collected the data is not named in ggm.

Description: Correlations among the 14 intelligence subtests of the Intelligence and Development Scales-2 in its standardization and validation sample (N = 1,991).
Reference: Grieder, S., & Grob, A. (2019). Exploratory factor analyses of the Intelligence and Development Scales-2: Implications for theory and practice. Assessment. https://doi.org/10.1177/1073191119845051
Notes: Covariance layout (irw_cov). Script data/covariance/batch_rpackages2.R. Taken from EFAtools::IDS2_R (package transcription, not verified against the paper); reshaped to the long lower triangle on 2026-11-17, values unchanged. 14 intelligence subtests of the IDS-2 (Grob & Hagmann-von Arx, 2018, Hogrefe); abbreviations in the EFAtools help page.

Description: Correlations among 24 bipolar trait-adjective rating scales from the interpersonal domain (523 students rating stereotypical persons).
Reference: Griffith, D., & Mulaik, S. A. (1998). Personality trait factors from the interpersonal domain. Poster, Society for Multivariate Experimental Psychology.
Notes: Covariance layout (irw_cov). Script data/covariance/batch_rpackages2.R. Taken from GPArotation::GriffithMulaik (package transcription, not verified against the paper); reshaped to the long lower triangle on 2026-11-17, values unchanged. 24 of 52 bipolar trait-adjective scales, four per hypothesised factor.

Description: Correlations among economic stress, depressed affect, withdrawal intentions, social ties and background variables for 262 entrepreneurs (Hayes's ESTRESS example).
Reference: Pollack, J. M., Vanepps, E. M., & Hayes, A. F. (2012). The moderating role of social ties on entrepreneurs' depressed affect and withdrawal intentions in response to economic stress. Journal of Organizational Behavior, 33(6), 789-810.
Notes: Covariance layout (irw_cov). Script data/covariance/batch_rpackages2.R. Taken from psychTools::Pollack (package transcription, not verified against the paper); reshaped to the long lower triangle on 2026-11-17, values unchanged. The ESTRESS example of Hayes (2013).

Description: Correlations among the 14 Spanish WAIS-III subtests for the standardization sample (N = 1,369) and for four education levels.
Reference: Colom, R., Abad, F. J., Garcia, L. F., & Juan-Espinosa, M. (2002). Education, Wechsler's Full Scale IQ, and g. Intelligence, 30, 449-462.
Notes: Covariance layout (irw_cov). Script data/covariance/batch_rpackages2.R. Taken from psychTools::colom (package transcription, not verified against the paper); reshaped to the long lower triangle on 2026-11-17, values unchanged. Whole sample; groups ed0-ed3 are its four education levels.
